gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Ionic's '11-year warranty' gives free repair only in years 0–5. Years 5–8 cost $175 per battery for repair or replacement, and years 8–11 give only a 30% discount on a replacement. Ionic also counts a battery as 'good' down to 70% of its original capacity, and it rates its 4,500 cycles at 80% depth of discharge, not 100%.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Ionic trolling-motor collection page (ionicbatteries.com/lithium-deep-cycle-batteries/trolling-motor-batteries/). It lists 'Warranty: 11 years' for every model and defines cycle life as 80% DoD until capacity falls below 80%. It does not mention the $175 fee for years 5–8, the 30% discount for years 8–11 or the 70% capacity point. ChatGPT's answer repeats '11-year warranty' for both Dakota and Ionic as if the two were the same. The cited Wired2Fish guide returned HTTP 403, so I could not check what it says about warranty terms. That is why I scored 2 and not 3. The uncited top results (thesweetandsimplekitchen, minormania, floridafishingkayaks and others) were not opened.
decides: This weakens Ionic's case as ChatGPT's 'best smart premium option' on warranty. Its headline 11 years is really 5 years of free coverage. The 11-year Dakota claim and the 10-year Battle Born claim may not be like-for-like either, but I could not open their terms (see unsourced). The page should compare free-coverage years and the cycle rating at one depth of discharge, not the headline years. On the sourced numbers alone, 4,500 cycles at 80% DoD works out to about 3,600 full cycles' worth of energy.

findings.label: Warranty, years 0–5
findings.value: Free repair. Replacement only 'if repair is not possible'. Customer pays shipping
findings.note: Applies to deep-cycle batteries of 12V 30Ah and up, which carry the 11-year warranty

findings.label: Warranty, years 5–8
findings.value: $175 per battery service charge to repair or replace
findings.note: Quote: 'Ionic Batteries will repair or replace battery with a service charge of $175 per battery.'

findings.label: Warranty, years 8–11
findings.value: 30% discount on a similar product, valid for 30 days
findings.note: No repair or replacement in these years, only the discount offer. The policy also excludes batteries left uncharged for more than 365 days and says cycling 'more than 1 time daily' can bring on normal end of life early.

findings.label: Capacity the warranty counts as good
findings.note: Quote: 'considered good at 70% of its original 100% SOC capacity'. Ionic's cycle-life rating, by contrast, runs to 80% capacity.

findings.label: Rated cycle life
findings.value: 4,500 cycles at 80% DoD, until capacity drops below 80%
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: The collection page defines cycle life as 'Full charge and discharge cycles at 80% depth of discharge before capacity drops below 80%.' Normalised to 100% DoD: 4,500 × 0.8 = 3,600 full-cycle equivalents ≈ 4,608 kWh delivered (× 1.28 kWh nominal). The product page also says '3,000 to 5,000 cycles'.

findings.label: Continuous and peak discharge
findings.value: 100 A continuous, 350 A peak for 3 s
findings.note: Spec table. Group 31, 13 × 6.75 × 9 in. The page gives weight as 29 lb in the spec table, 28 lb in the description and 24 lb in the FAQ.

findings.label: Price
findings.note: Maker's US store. Listed as in stock, can be backordered.

findings.label: Cycle life and discharge
findings.value: 3,000 cycles at 80% DoD to 80% capacity. 50 A continuous, 350 A peak for 3 s. $799
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: From the same comparison table. Within one brand, cycle ratings run from 3,000 (36V 50Ah) to 5,000 (36V 75Ah).
